summary: This class models a traffic light that cycles through Red, Green, and Yellow. It remembers its current color, can advance to the next color, and can report whether a driver must stop.

lines.text: The light's current color is stored as private state, starting at Red so every new TrafficLight begins in a known, safe condition.
A getter lets other code read the color without being able to change it directly, which keeps the class in control of its own state.
This method moves the light on to its next color; it returns nothing because its whole job is to change the object's state.
Writing the literal first means equals is called on a value that can never be null, a common Java habit that avoids NullPointerException.
Red gives way to Green, which is the first step of the cycle.
The second branch handles the middle of the cycle, so each color is checked in the order the light actually follows.
Green gives way to Yellow rather than straight to Red, matching how a real light warns drivers.
The final else catches Yellow (and any unexpected value), guaranteeing that advance always leaves the light in a valid color.
A method that returns a boolean answers a yes-or-no question about the object, which makes it easy to assert on in a test.
Stopping is required for every color except Green, so the logic is expressed as one negated comparison instead of listing Red and Yellow separately.
